bibliographic.title: Electronic Governance Controls for AI-Enabled Agentic Large Language Models in Digital Government (Compliance-by-Design and Evidence-Linked Evaluation)
bibliographic.venue: International Journal of Research and Studies Publishing
bibliographic.citation_apa: Almaghrabi, M. A. (2026). Electronic governance controls for AI-enabled agentic large language models in digital government (Compliance-by-design and evidence-linked evaluation). International Journal of Research and Studies Publishing, 7(80).

methodology.study_design: conceptual framework proposal grounded in documentary analysis, official maturity indicators, flagship platform vignette, and open-data KPI baseline
methodology.sample_description: policy and governance evidence across digital-government strategies, data-governance and privacy instruments, public-sector AI initiatives, official digital-government maturity indicators, a flagship platform vignette, and a government complaint-escalation KPI series
methodology.technology_context: LLM-enabled agentic AI systems in digital government under binding regulatory constraints (Saudi Arabia; Vision 2030; SDAIA-led transformation)

eligibility.decision_rationale: The provided text strongly addresses governance, accountability, privacy, auditability, compliance-by-design, and human-in-the-loop controls for LLM-enabled agentic systems in regulated public-sector digital government. However, no explicit conversational AI, chatbot, or conversational-system evidence appears in the supplied excerpts, so it is better classified as supporting rather than central evidence for a conversational-governance-focused review. Full-text confirmation is needed because only front matter and partial introduction were supplied.
eligibility.manual_spotcheck_reason: Only pages 1-2 were provided; conversational-AI relevance, methods detail, limitations, and peer-review status require full-text verification.

appraisal.notes: Appraisal is based only on abstract and partial introduction. The study clearly states a framework objective and qualitative documentary analysis with triangulation, but sampling boundaries, analytic procedure, ethics, limitations, and detailed findings are not visible in the supplied text.

cerqual.explanation: The abstract presents a coherent governance framework for agentic LLMs in digital government with named controls and evaluation dimensions, but methodological detail, limitations, and conversational-system specificity are insufficient in the provided excerpt to support high confidence.

coding.theme: Governance controls for agentic LLMs in digital government
rq_alignment: governance of generative AI in regulated contexts
risk and accountability in public-sector AI deployment

synthesis.main_claim: Public-sector use of LLM-enabled agentic systems requires an electronic-governance framework that enforces accountability, privacy, and auditability through bounded autonomy and compliance-by-design controls.
synthesis.contribution: Proposes an evaluation-ready input-process-output framework for assessing productivity, decision quality, and auditable compliance, supported by documentary analysis, maturity indicators, a flagship platform vignette, and an open-data KPI baseline.
synthesis.use_in_review: Use as supporting evidence on governance, compliance, auditability, and human-in-the-loop controls for agentic LLM systems in regulated digital-government settings; verify full text before treating as central evidence for conversational governance.

evidence.claim: Study proposes an electronic-governance framework for governed use of LLM-enabled agentic systems under binding constraints.
evidence.excerpt: This paper aims to propose an electronic- governance framework that enables governed use of LLM-enabled agentic systems under binding constraints.

evidence.claim: Method uses qualitative documentary analysis with triangulation.
evidence.excerpt: Through qualitative documentary analysis, the study examines policy and governance evidence across digital-government strategies, data-governance and privacy instruments, and public- sector AI initiatives.

evidence.claim: Empirical grounding includes maturity indicators, a vignette, and a KPI baseline.
evidence.excerpt: Empirical grounding is strengthened through triangulation with official digital- government maturity indicators, a flagship platform vignette illustrating operational scalability, and a reproducible open-data key performance indicator (KPI) baseline derived from a government complaint-escalation series.

evidence.claim: Core governance controls include audit logging and human-in-the-loop gating.
evidence.excerpt: bounded autonomy implemented through allowlisted tools, controlled state and memory, verification and feedback loops, role-based access control, audit logging, and human-in-the-loop gating.
